clue.text: Cry out for a round of drinks

definitions.meaning: to cry out is to yell or bellow
in a British pub, your turn to buy everyone's drinks is called this

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a loud yell; the other is British slang for a person's turn to buy drinks for the group.

clue.text: Kind of grouse flying round mid Kent

indicators.note: the scrambled bird letters go round the middle of the county name
flying sends the letters of grouse scattering into a new order
mid asks for the central letters of the word Kent

explanation.surface: A game bird takes off and circles over the middle of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' looks like the noun 'a type of', as if a kind of grouse were meant, but it is the adjective for open-handed; 'mid Kent' takes only the two central letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a kind person is open-handed and giving.

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A mother and her child go looking for fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link: the wordplay is what you are after to find the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small dark-purple plum.

definitions.meaning: to hold something is to retain it
the strongest central tower of a castle, its last stronghold

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to retain possession; the other is a castle's fortified inner tower.

clue.text: I am in a class of Latin brilliance

indicators.note: the clue's I says it is placed inside the following word, the class

parts.note: genus is the Latin word for a class or kind, used in biology
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boast of brilliance at Latin by someone top of the class.
explanation.walkthrough: GENUS, Latin for 'kind' and the biological rank above species, takes I inside it. 'class' seems to mean a school class, which suits the boast.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: exceptional intellectual brilliance or talent.

indicators.note: goods imported from abroad are shipped and repacked, so the letters of the country name come in rearranged

explanation.surface: A fruit shipped in from Argentina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imported from' rearranges the nine letters of ARGENTINE; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small loose-skinned orange-like citrus.

clue.text: A smoker he is a reformed snob

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters of a smoker he are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A smoker who has given up is a reformed snob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' rearranges A SMOKER HE. 'snob' is an old dialect word for a cobbler, which a reformed smoker certainly is not.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic sense: before it meant a social climber, the word was a dialect name for a cobbler.

clue.text: Courage to take tea in repast

indicators.note: in says the drink's letter sits inside the word for the repast

parts.note: a repast is a meal
tea is spelt T, its letter name

explanation.surface: It takes nerve to drink tea at a formal dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes in MEAL; 'to take' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic sense: this spelling once also meant mettle, spirit or courage.

clue.text: Keep on complaining about pills starting flu

indicators.note: about means surrounding: the moaning word goes round the first letter of pills

parts.note: to gripe is to grumble persistently

indicators.note: starting means only the opening letter of pills is used

explanation.surface: A patient keeps grumbling about pills as flu sets in.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an old French name for influenza.

indicators.note: in says that letter goes inside the word dress
first means only the opening letter of the word up is used

explanation.surface: Getting dressed up for an occasion under compulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress up' looks like one phrase; U, the first letter of 'up', goes in DRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: threats or pressure used to force someone to act.

definitions.meaning: British slang for a prison sentence, the time served by inmates of the pen

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the oat breakfast dish; the other is British slang for doing time in jail, a stretch for prisoners.

definitions.meaning: to badger is to pester or harass someone

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is hunting dogs; the other is a verb, as harasses or pesters.

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet, telling someone to be still
a rub is a massage

explanation.surface: A gardener's bush keeps quiet while getting a massage.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a woody plant smaller than a tree.

clue.text: It is used to make a pasty with last of flour

definitions.text: It is used to make a pasty with last of flour

indicators.note: make means put together, so the letters are made into a new word
last of means only the final letter of flour is taken

explanation.surface: Instructions for a pasty, finished with the last of the flour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' rearranges PASTY with R, the final letter of 'flour'. The whole clue also describes what a pasty is made from.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasty is a baked case of dough round a filling, so the dough is what makes it.

indicators.note: to reform is to shape anew, so the letters of education are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone told off the reform of education.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: warned or reprimanded.

definitions.meaning: to pocket is to take or claim something for oneself

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is loose trousers; the other is a verb meaning claims or takes for oneself.

definitions.meaning: to wait at table, attending diners
to assist or be of use

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is attending at table as a waiter does; the other is giving aid or being useful.

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of that's is used

parts.note: handy means convenient

explanation.surface: A drink that's convenient at the end of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: beer mixed with lemonade, a British pub drink.

indicators.note: doesn't half says only half the name of the game remains, the other half dropped

parts.note: table tennis, whose informal name is a doubled rhyming word

explanation.surface: British idiom: the game really smells, doesn't half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't half' is British for 'really does', but here it takes away half of PING-PONG. The answer is British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a stench or bad odour.

clue.text: Exclamation of disdain over loop the loop

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the two loop words are read backwards

parts.note: a hoop is a loop or ring
a second hoop, again a loop or ring

explanation.surface: An aerobatic pilot sneers at the loop the loop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loop the loop' gives HOOP and HOOP, and 'over' turns the whole run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A dismissive interjection, also used as a verb for scornfully rejecting an idea.

clue.text: To enter up first class return to paradise

indicators.note: enter says the word to goes inside the word up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: return means the first class piece is read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first class, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Travelling first class on the way back to paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: TO enters UP to give UTOP; A1, first class, with 1 as I, read backwards gives IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an imagined perfect place, an ideal society.

definitions.meaning: to pelt someone repeatedly, as with questions or shot
a hot spice ground from peppercorns

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to pelt with many missiles; the other is the hot spice from peppercorns.

clue.text: Local argument for ancient burial mound

parts.note: the local is a British term for one's nearby pub, which has a bar
a row is a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: A dispute in the local pub over an ancient burial mound.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaeological term: a prehistoric earth heap over a grave.

indicators.note: climber, in a down clue, means the hill word goes upwards and is read backwards

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
ate means took, as food

explanation.surface: A hill climber took a spin.
explanation.walkthrough: TOR is a craggy hill in south-west England; read upwards it gives ROT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to turn round on an axis.

definitions.meaning: a shady arbour or secluded spot in a garden
a violinist draws a bow, so one who bows

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a shady garden arbour; the other is jokingly one who bows, like a violinist.

indicators.note: detail means take off the tail, the last letter of the word come

parts.note: padre is a name for a priest or chaplain, a father

explanation.surface: A friend asks a father to come and give details.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detail' looks like 'give particulars' but means cut off the tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a comrade or buddy, from Spanish.

clue.text: Still a bird of paradise by back garden

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the garden of Eden; a bird is slang for a woman

indicators.note: back means only the last letter of garden is used

explanation.surface: A bird of paradise still sits by the back garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird of paradise' looks like the exotic species, but it is Eve, a 'bird' (woman) in Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: used for emphasis, as in even better meaning still better.

clue.text: Strong wind drops round son of typhoeus

indicators.note: drops means the letter is let fall out of the storm word

parts.note: a typhoon is a violent tropical storm
round means a circle, the letter O

explanation.surface: A strong wind drops around the child of a mythic monster.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a monstrous giant, closely linked to and sometimes said to descend from the storm giant Typhoeus.

clue.text: It goes on ahead of the queen in a flutter

indicators.note: in places the queen's letters inside the gamble

parts.note: a flutter is British slang for a small bet
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Something goes on ahead of the queen during a flutter.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'ahead' as 'a head': the hat goes on one. 'ahead of' looks like a position indicator, but 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft round flat cap is worn on a head.

definitions.meaning: a fast warship, a naval craft
one who wrecks or ruins things

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a fast naval warship; the other is anyone who wrecks or ruins.
